- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day high), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 3–5 days after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; apply a 2–4 day lag correction to downward moves.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 5 days by 1–2% relative to 10-day moving average.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction for next 3–7 days.
